Interactive preview · sample data · Preview only · nothing changes on your server

Try it: open Arrange widgets, then move, resize or add a card. This is a simplified demo, not your server.

With JavaScript disabled, the preview remains a static example. The guides and screenshots still work.

FROM INSTALL TO EVERYDAY USE

Easy to start. Room to grow.
  1. 1Install on your server

    Choose Docker, Unraid, Synology or TrueNAS below. Follow the guide for storage, permissions and starting AIO.

  2. 2Choose your apps

    Create your administrator account and follow the setup wizard. Pick the media server and tools you need; add more later.

  3. 3Let AIO connect them

    AIO configures supported connections, download clients and library folders. Your provider details and media sources remain yours to supply.

  4. 4Make it your own

    Open your apps from one dashboard. Arrange widgets and configure backups, updates and advanced options when you need them.

Choose your server ↓

Already running a media stack? Review the advanced guides before changing your setup.

HOME, YOUR WAY

Make room for what matters.

Your Home screen is yours to arrange. Try the controls in the preview above, then do the same in AIO.

Try the widget demo ↑
  1. 1 Open the layout editor

    On Home, choose the four-block layout icon next to the page tabs. Widget handles and an editing toolbar appear.

  2. 2 Move things around

    Drag a widget to its new place. On a phone, drag its grip so you can still scroll the page.

  3. 3 Find the right size

    Drag the lower-right corner, or open a widget’s settings and choose a size. Remove a widget there too.

  4. 4 Add it. Make it yours.

    Choose Add widget, pick This size or Every size, then choose a widget. Changes save automatically; choose Done when finished.

Phone, tablet and desktop can each have their own layout. Empty widgets may disappear outside edit mode until their connected app has something to show.

THE CATALOG

The tools you love. One place to run them.

Browse Discover, My apps and categories in the sidebar. Choose Open to launch an app; choose its name or icon to see its settings.

Learn the dashboard →

LESS FUSS. MORE CONTROL.

Set it up once.

Grouped settings with search. Find your profile and appearance under Personal, connections under Connections, and updates and backups under Maintenance.

Learn the dashboard →

LET’S GET YOU SET UP

Start with your server.

Pick the name you recognise. We’ll take it from there, one step at a time.

▤ Unraid

Have an Unraid server? Start with the template and SSD download setup.

↗ ▥ Synology

Using a Synology NAS? Install Container Manager first, then create one project.

↗ ▰ Docker

Running Docker elsewhere? Use the single-container setup.

↗ ▧ TrueNAS

Using TrueNAS SCALE? Follow the custom app setup.

↗ ✳ New to this? Start here

No need to know every app or every setting. The install guide explains what you need, what to click, and what you should see next.

Read the install guide ↗

Advanced setup →

FAQ

A few things worth knowing. Do I need every app?

No. Start with a media server and the tools you actually need. Add more later from Catalog.

Where do my movies and shows go?

They stay on your server. SSD download staging can speed up downloading and unpacking; the main library can stay on your HDDs.

Do I need a VPN or public domain?

Neither is required to start on your home network. Both can be configured later.

Is this a working server in my browser?

No. The dashboard is a visual demo with sample data. Catalog and Settings show real AIO screenshots. Nothing here connects to your server.

Your media. A calmer home for it.

Self-hosted. Open source. Built to bring your home media tools together.

docs.title: Your first AIO installation
docs.text:
You do not need to install every app or understand Docker to choose the right guide. Start with the server you already have.

What you are installing

AIO is one application that manages several media tools inside one container (a packaged app running on your server). Install AIO once. Add Sonarr, Radarr, Jellyfin and download clients from AIO → Catalog, rather than installing separate containers for them.

docs.title: 1. Pick your server
docs.text:
Follow one guide below. Do not run commands from all the guides.

Your server Start here Check this first Unraid Unraid setup Array started; SSD/NVMe pool mounted for fast downloads Synology NAS Synology setup Container Manager installed and running; let DSM create the docker folder TrueNAS SCALE TrueNAS setup Permission to create a custom app and storage folders Another computer with Docker Docker setup Docker and Docker Compose installed and running Debian, Ubuntu or Proxmox LXC without Docker Native Linux setup Comfortable administering a Linux server

A NAS is a network storage server. If you are reading this on a laptop, the server is usually a separate device. Run installation commands on that device; open the dashboard from your laptop or phone afterward.

docs.title: 2. Know where your files will go
docs.text:
The platform guide creates the right folders for you. Do not copy placeholder paths from a different platform.

Folder What it holds Keep in mind Config App settings, accounts and databases Keep backups of this folder Download staging Files being downloaded or unpacked SSD/NVMe helps here; leave room for downloading and extraction Finished torrents Completed torrents that may still be seeding Can stay on HDD storage Media library Your organised films, shows and other media Can stay on large HDDs Backups Saved configuration backups Prefer a separate disk or backup destination

A host path is a folder on your NAS. A container path, such as /data/media, is how AIO sees that folder inside the container. They refer to the same files through a folder mapping; do not create a second library because the path looks different.

SSD downloads and an HDD library can work together. Follow the folders in your platform guide; custom storage is covered under Advanced.

Leave the defaults alone at first

Keep the paths and ports from your platform guide unless they conflict with something already running. A VPN, domain name and Cloudflare account are optional. You can add them later.

docs.title: 3. Open AIO
docs.text:
Once your platform guide says the container is running, open this address in a browser:

http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8080

Replace YOUR-SERVER-IP with your NAS/server's address, for example http://192.168.1.50:8080. That address is only an example; use the address shown by your router or NAS. If you changed the host port, use that port instead of 8080.

You should see: the AIO account-creation screen. Create your administrator account with a username, email and password. If you see a login screen instead, an account already exists; sign in with that account.

docs.title: 4. Finish the setup wizard
docs.text:
1. Choose only the apps you need. A small starting point is Jellyfin for playback, plus the automation/download tools you actually use.
  2. Enter a Usenet provider account only if you chose a Usenet downloader. AIO does not supply a Usenet subscription.
  3. Leave VPN and remote access off unless you are ready to configure them.
  4. Finish the wizard and wait for installation. Open Catalog and look for Running on your chosen apps.
  5. Choose Open UI on an app to finish its own setup. Jellyfin/Plex can need their own account and library settings; the AIO account does not replace them.

You should see: Home, Catalog and Settings in AIO, with your chosen apps listed in Catalog. A first download of an app can take time. If an app stays stopped or fails, open its logs rather than repeatedly reinstalling it.

docs.title: 5. Make Home your own
docs.text: Try the visual widget example, then follow the dashboard guide. It shows the layout button, adding widgets, moving them and changing their size. An empty Home does not necessarily mean something is broken: many widgets need a connected app with content first.

docs.title: If you get stuck
docs.text: What you see What to do next Browser cannot connect Confirm AIO is running. Check the server IP and mapped host port. Use the same home network first. Port already in use Another app is using that host port. Change the host side of the mapping in your platform settings, then open the new port. Permission denied Follow the ownership step in your platform guide. PUID/PGID are the numeric user/group IDs AIO uses; they must be allowed to write to the folders. Synology docker folder missing Install and start DSM Container Manager first. Do not make the docker shared folder manually before installation. Home widget empty Check Catalog for the app it depends on, then the widget help in Using the dashboard. Download speed low Check whether active downloads/unpacking land on HDDs or SSD. Use the storage options in your NAS guide. Open UI cannot connect Check that app is running and its port is published (advanced port reference).

docs.title: Updates and optional remote access
docs.text:
Updating AIO and updating the apps inside it are different actions:

  • AIO: follow your platform's container update flow. Pull the new image and recreate the container while keeping the same folder mappings. A restart alone does not apply a new image.
  • Managed apps: use Settings → Updates in AIO. Automatic schedules default to off.
  • Remote access: configure Cloudflare Tunnel, then Cloudflare Access. Start locally before adding this.

Technical reference material is kept separately under Advanced.

docs.title: Advanced: ports and settings
docs.text: Beginner guide · Advanced

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
The manager UI uses 8080. Child apps listen inside the same container. Compose and NAS templates publish those ports on the host so Open UI works (http://YOUR-IP:8989 for Sonarr, and so on). Host networking is an alternative if you prefer not to map each port.

Application Default port Manager UI 8080 qBittorrent 8081 Shelfmark 8084 SABnzbd 8085 Jellyfin 8096 Flaresolverr 8191 (x86_64 only) Bazarr 6767 NZBGet 6789 Lidarr 8686 Sonarr 8989 Radarr 7878 Prowlarr 9696 Seerr 5055 Grimmory 6060 NeutArr 9705 Cleanuparr 11011 Recyclarr none (CLI only) Plex 32400

docs.title: Common environment variablesDonate
docs.text:
Copy .env.example for native installs. Many of these can also be set later in Settings.

Variable Purpose PUID / PGID User the apps run as (match folder ownership) TZ / AMM_TIMEZONE Timezone for logs and schedules AMM_DOWNLOAD_DIR / AMM_MEDIA_DIR Paths inside the container (change host mounts in compose) GITHUB_TOKEN Optional; higher GitHub API limits for updates AMM_CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_* Optional remote tunnel (cloudflared starts after apps on boot) AMM_VPN_* Optional VPN for qBittorrent, Prowlarr, and Flaresolverr (they wait for the tunnel; local DNS cache for those apps) AMM_SECURE_COOKIES Set to true when the manager is served over HTTPS; default false for LAN HTTP. AMM_PREFLIGHT_MIN_FREE_MB Minimum free MiB required on storage paths before installation/update; default 512. AMM_BACKUP_RECOVERY_TOKEN Optional operator recovery secret of at least 32 characters, only before a working admin account. Remove after recovery; see the security guide.

docs.title: Using AIO, step by step
docs.text: Start here once you can open AIO in your browser. First get one app working; add more when you need them.

docs.title: 1. Finish your first setup
docs.text: Create the administrator account, then complete the wizard. For a small start, choose Jellyfin to play media you already own. Leave VPN and access from outside your home off until everything works locally. Wait until the chosen app says Running in Catalog.

docs.title: 2. Know the three pages
docs.text:
AIO Home See downloads, upcoming releases and server information. You can arrange the widgets yourself. Catalog Install apps, see whether they are running and choose Open to open an app. Settings Change AIO’s appearance, account and updates. This is not where you add films to a media server.

Header: Home, Catalog and Settings stay centered across the full header. On narrow screens they have their own centered row. The header scrolls with the page. On Home, the four-block layout button is on the right, beside your account. All app pages, controls and labels use Figtree; when that web font cannot load, the same system-font fallback is used throughout.

docs.title: Using the new catalog
docs.text:
Open Catalog at the top. The left sidebar helps you choose what to see; the apps appear on the right.

Sidebar option What you see Discover Featured apps and the complete catalog. My apps Apps you have already installed, including stopped apps. Active Only apps that are running. Available Apps you can install. Search / Category Find an app by name or choose a type of app.

Use the sort control above the app list for Popularity or A to Z. Missing an app? Clear the search and choose Discover to remove the status/category selection.

To start with Jellyfin: search for Jellyfin. Choose Install if it is not installed, wait for Running, then choose Open. If it is installed but stopped, choose Start first. Open launches Jellyfin in its own browser tab.

Click an app’s name, icon or row to open its app settings popup. This does not open the app itself. The ⋯ button offers Settings, Stop, Restart, Logs, Update and Uninstall as applicable. Close the popup with × or Escape. Only save changes when you intend to change that app.

Catalog app settings change one app. The Settings page in the top navigation changes AIO itself: profile, appearance, connections, backups and updates.

docs.title: Find your way around Settings
docs.text:
The settings page uses the same sidebar-and-content layout as the catalog. On a computer, choose a group and page on the left; the selected page appears on the right. The search field filters the menu, not the values of your settings. Scroll the sidebar to find lower groups. On a phone, open Settings sections and choose a page.

What do you want to change? Choose this page Name, profile photo or password Personal → Profile Language, theme or wallpaper Personal → Language and appearance App dock or sign-in message Dashboard → Start page Update an app Maintenance → Updates Make a settings backup Maintenance → Backups Find why a widget is empty System → Help and diagnostics API keys, TV or Homey connections Connections → App connections

The sidebar only selects a page. Change a setting on the right and use that section’s Save button when shown. Arrange widgets directly on Home, using the four-block layout button; Start page settings control the dock and sign-in text.

docs.title: 3. Open your first app
docs.text:
Choose Catalog, find Jellyfin and choose Open. Complete Jellyfin’s own setup if requested. When it asks for library folders, use /data/media/movies for films and /data/media/tv for shows with the default installation. Those names refer to the media folders already connected by your platform guide. Do not create another copy because your NAS shows a different folder path.

Check: Jellyfin opens in its own browser tab. A folder without media will look empty; that is normal.

docs.title: 4. Play your first film
docs.text:
Use a film file you already own, for example MyFilm.mp4. Copy it into the movies folder on your server, not into the Downloads folder and not into the website demo.

Server Where to copy the file Synology In DSM File Station: home → aio-media-manager → media → movies. Choose Upload and select the file from your computer. Unraid Open the aio-media-manager network share, then media → movies. The last step of the Unraid guide explains enabling that private share. TrueNAS Open the aio-media network share, then media → movies. Step 7 in the TrueNAS guide sets up access. Docker on Linux On the server, open your home folder → aio-media-manager → media → movies. From another computer you can copy over SSH with scp as shown below.

For a remote Linux server: run this on your computer, replacing the file path, username and server IP. The example copies to the standard home-folder installation.

On Windows a file path may look like C:\Users\Alex\Videos\MyFilm.mp4; on macOS it may look like /Users/alex/Movies/MyFilm.mp4. Keep the quotes around your actual path. Use the same server username and IP that you used for SSH.

scp "/PATH/TO/YOUR/FILM.mp4" YOUR-USER@SERVER-IP:aio-media-manager/media/movies/

For a series, use media/tv instead. After copying, open Jellyfin → Dashboard → Libraries and choose Scan All Libraries (or the scan action for your library). Return to the Jellyfin home screen, open the film and choose Play.

Check: the film appears and starts playing. If it does not appear, verify the server file is in the same folder you selected in Jellyfin, then scan again.

docs.title: 5. Arrange your Home widgets
docs.text:
1The edit buttonHomeCatalogSettings●

On Home, choose the four-block layout icon on the right of the header, beside your account. Widget handles and an editing toolbar appear.

2Move: drag the grip⠿×Downloading↘

Resize: drag this corner

3Choose what to add＋ Add widgetDone

Choose Add widget, pick This size or Every size, then choose a widget. Changes save automatically; choose Done when finished.

Arrange your Home widgets

These pictures explain the real controls. The website example uses sample data; it cannot change your actual dashboard.

docs.title: Why is a widget empty?
docs.text: First check that the related app is running in Catalog. Recently added needs media in Jellyfin/Plex; the calendar needs scheduled titles from your connected apps. An empty widget can disappear outside editing mode. Adding a widget does not install the app it needs.

docs.title: 6. What are the other apps for?
docs.text:
App Jellyfin / Plex Play your existing media. Sonarr / Radarr Organise shows / films and automate downloads you choose. SABnzbd / NZBGet Download from Usenet; this needs your own provider account. qBittorrent Download and seed torrents. Prowlarr Manage the search sources used by the automation apps.

You do not need all of them. Add an app from Catalog only when you know what you want it to do. The detailed connection steps are under Advanced.

docs.title: 7. Keep apps up to date
docs.text: Use Settings → Updates for the apps inside AIO. Updating AIO itself is a separate action in your NAS/Docker interface; the platform’s advanced guide explains that. Make a configuration backup in Settings → Backups before changing a working setup.

docs.title: Screens and technical reference
docs.text: Screens and technical reference.

docs.title: Checks, progress and recovery
docs.text:
Before an install or manual update, AIO shows storage, maintenance and download-access checks. Resolve any blocking result before continuing. Catalog → Installation activity shows stages and opens live logs; close and reopen it as needed. If setup fails after installation, Try again retries starting and connecting the app.

In Settings → App connections, choose Check my installation to read back the actual configuration. Auto-Wire applies automatic configuration; the check itself changes no app settings. Public starter indexers require an explicit opt-in.

Settings → Backups supports encrypted HTTPS/WebDAV copies and safe restore tests in a temporary folder. Keep the encryption password outside the server. Settings → Notifications adds disk warning/recovery thresholds and recent incidents. Recyclarr app settings include Manual configuration to preserve edited YAML exactly.

See installation checks and recovery and sessions, HTTPS and emergency access.

docs.title: Using the dashboard — Advanced
docs.text:
Advanced

This is the technical reference. For a first installation, follow the beginner guide instead. Beginner guide.

This guide is for after AIO is installed and you can open the web UI.

Goal

Finish the wizard for the apps you need, use Home day to day, and use Open on Catalog whenever you want that tool’s screen.

Default address on your home network:

http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8080

Replace the IP (and port, if you changed it).

docs.title: First time
docs.text:
1. Create the admin account when prompted (username, email, password).
  2. Finish the first-run wizard: the apps you want, a Usenet server if you use one, optional VPN, and an optional Cloudflare Tunnel. The wizard installs that selection. The tunnel and the VPN start as soon as it finishes, when you turned them on.
  3. After a container recreate, the dashboard answers while apps are still starting. With VPN on, qBittorrent, Prowlarr, and Flaresolverr wait until the WireGuard handshake is up (AIO retries the VPN if the first try fails). Cloudflare Tunnel starts last, after the apps answer, so cloudflared does not log connection refused against origins that are not listening yet.
  4. Wait until Catalog shows those apps as running. Use Open for anything that still has its own account (Plex, Jellyfin, NZBGet).
  5. Add more later from Catalog. You do not need every app.

Start small (for example Radarr + one download client + Jellyfin), then add the rest.

Header: Home, Catalog and Settings stay centered across the full header. On narrow screens they have their own centered row. The header scrolls with the page. On Home, the four-block layout button is on the right, beside your account. All app pages, controls and labels use Figtree; when that web font cannot load, the same system-font fallback is used throughout.

docs.title: Arrange your Home widgets
docs.text:
1The edit buttonHomeCatalogSettings●

On Home, choose the four-block layout icon on the right of the header, beside your account. Widget handles and an editing toolbar appear.

2Move: drag the grip⠿×Downloading↘

Resize: drag this corner

3Choose what to add＋ Add widgetDone

Choose Add widget, pick This size or Every size, then choose a widget. Changes save automatically; choose Done when finished.

Try the interactive example

This is a visual explanation of the real controls; the website demo uses sample data and simplified movement.

Click a widget while editing to open its size choices. The × removes it from the selected screen size; use Undo immediately if you removed the wrong one.

Changes save automatically to your AIO profile; Done closes editing. A separate phone/tablet/desktop layout means changing desktop does not always change your phone. The size buttons only appear when the window can preview those sizes.

Dashboard

For an empty card, first check its source app in Catalog. Settings → Help and diagnostics → Explain empty widgets can show why content is missing. Settings → Start page also controls the app dock; Settings → Language and appearance changes the look.

On a keyboard: Tab to a widget while editing; arrow keys move it, Shift + arrows resize, Enter opens size choices, and Delete removes it.

docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Home is a grid. Phone, tablet, and desktop each keep their own layout (4, 8, and 12 columns). The layout control on the Home tab moves, resizes, adds, and removes widgets. Settings → Start page shows or hides the app dock and sets the sign-in message. Keys are under Settings → App connections.

Widget What it shows Greeting Time of day Search Seerr search Calendar Upcoming episodes and movies. A season that lands on one day is one entry Downloading Active downloads, with pause all / resume all. Stuck items can be removed Recently added New shows and movies. Scrolling loads further Jellyfin pages. Plex stays on its latest 20 Requests Seerr requests that are not finished, plus ones marked available or declined in the last 30 days Trending Seerr's trending list. Scrolling keeps loading Now playing Who is watching on Jellyfin or Plex, including direct play Storage Disk use for config, downloads, and media Server CPU, memory, and network. With host /sys mounted at /host/sys, this is the server's network cards. Without that mount it is only this container's traffic Needs attention The same checks as Settings → Notifications, with a link to fix each one Other downloads Off by default; add it from the layout control. What SABnzbd, NZBGet, and qBittorrent downloaded that is not a film or series (music, books, games, software, archives), each with an icon for its kind

Install, start, stop, and Open live on Catalog. The dock at the bottom of Home opens apps that are already installed.

LAN Open usually looks like http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8989 (example for Sonarr). If you set up Cloudflare public hostnames, Open can instead use https://sonarr.yourdomain.com — see Cloudflare Tunnel.

docs.title: What the wizard wires
docs.text:
After an app is healthy — or when you click Auto-Wire — AIO sets download folders and categories, root folders and download clients in Sonarr, Radarr, and Lidarr, Prowlarr sync, Seerr, Bazarr pairing, and starter configs for Recyclarr and NeutArr. Settings → Usenet holds the news server and sends it to SABnzbd and NZBGet. Public starter indexers are off by default. Enable them explicitly in the wizard or Settings → App connections, then run Auto-Wire to add them. Disabling the choice keeps existing indexers. Remove any you do not want; they are not added back.

SSD staging and an HDD library are supported; imports across them copy files. Hardlinks require the same filesystem.

Still yours to finish:

  • A Plex account.
  • NeutArr's first-run setup token (below), until that account exists.
  • Signing in to Jellyfin and NZBGet. On the LAN, Open already signs in Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, qBittorrent, SABnzbd, Bazarr, and Seerr as the manager admin. Public hostnames always show the app's own login.
  • Seerr's admin and first-run wizard are completed for you from that shared login (through Jellyfin, or a claimed Plex).

VPN, Cloudflare Tunnel, Recyclarr, NeutArr, and backups are optional.

docs.title: NeutArr first-run setup token
docs.text:
The first time NeutArr starts, before it has an account, it asks for a one-time setup token.

  1. Wait until NeutArr shows as running.
  2. Open Catalog → NeutArr → Settings.
  3. Copy First-run setup token and paste it into NeutArr's setup screen.

That value is the file /config/neutarr/.setup-token inside the appliance (the host folder mounted as /config). NeutArr deletes the file after the account is created, and the Settings field goes empty. Until NeutArr has started, the field stays empty.

In Settings → App connections, choose Check my installation to read back the actual configuration. Auto-Wire applies automatic configuration; the check itself changes no app settings. Public starter indexers require an explicit opt-in.

Settings → Backups supports encrypted HTTPS/WebDAV copies and safe restore tests in a temporary folder. Keep the encryption password outside the server. Settings → Notifications adds disk warning/recovery thresholds and recent incidents. Recyclarr app settings include Manual configuration to preserve edited YAML exactly.

docs.title: Opening each app’s UI
docs.text:
Situation What to use At home on Wi‑Fi Open → http://IP:PORT Away from home with Cloudflare Open → https://subdomain.yourdomain.com You changed an app’s listen port AIO updates published routes; recreate the container if LAN links still look wrong. The manager port itself is compose/env (AMM_API_PORT), shown on Settings → Server and storage

If Open fails:

  • Is the app running on Catalog?
  • Are you on the same network (for LAN links)?
  • For HTTPS links: is the tunnel connected and was Publish successful? (Cloudflare guide)

docs.title: Using the new catalog
docs.text:
Open Catalog at the top. The left sidebar helps you choose what to see; the apps appear on the right.

Click an app’s name, icon or row to open its app settings popup. This does not open the app itself. The ⋯ button offers Settings, Stop, Restart, Logs, Update and Uninstall as applicable. Close the popup with × or Escape. Only save changes when you intend to change that app.

Catalog app settings change one app. The Settings page in the top navigation changes AIO itself: profile, appearance, connections, backups and updates.

The search field filters the menu, not the values of your settings. Scroll the sidebar to find lower groups. On a phone, open Settings sections and choose a page.

docs.title: Settings you will actually use
docs.text:
Names in the UI may be short labels; here is what they mean in practice.

Choose this page What do you want to change? Profile Your account, photo and password. Language and appearance Language, theme, wallpaper and branding. Start page App dock and sign-in message; widget layout is edited on Home. VPN The VPN connection for supported apps. External access Cloudflare Tunnel, public hostnames and trusted proxies. App connections Jellyfin/Seerr keys, TV pairing and read-only Homey connections. Usenet Usenet provider details for SABnzbd and NZBGet. Updates App updates and schedules. AIO itself is updated through your NAS/Docker. Backups Create, check, schedule and restore configuration backups. Notifications Email and Discord alerts. Server and storage Timezone, logs, permissions and storage paths. Change mounts on the host. Help and diagnostics Explain empty widgets and collect diagnostic information. About this app Version, install on your device and project support.

After changing important network or port settings, give apps a moment to reload — or restart AIO if links still look stale.

docs.title: Updating apps vs updating AIO
docs.text:
What How AIO itself (dashboard + supervisor) Pull a new Docker image and recreate the container (Install). Settings → Updates only tells you when :latest moved Installed apps (Sonarr, Seerr, and the rest) Settings → Updates. Update one app or all of them. Progress shows there, and Catalog and Home show Updating…. The dashboard keeps answering. Schedules default to off

The image does not bump those apps on its own. Read release notes on GitHub if something major changed.

docs.title: Common snags
docs.text: Problem Try this Blank or login loop on an app Clear site data for that URL; confirm the app is running NeutArr asks for a setup token Catalog → NeutArr → Settings after NeutArr is running. The token is removed once the NeutArr account exists Permission errors writing files Host folder owner must match the container user (PUID/PGID) Sonarr imports but duplicates files Downloads and media must share one filesystem for hardlinks Works at home, not on phone data Need Tunnel (+ ideally Access); LAN IPs are not reachable from mobile data Two Sonarrs fighting Remove any extra Sonarr container; only AIO should run it Server graph counts only this container Mount host /sys read-only at /host/sys and recreate (Docker) Jellyfin recently added looks short Scroll the rail — it loads further pages. If the rail stays empty, set a Jellyfin API key under Settings → App connections Plex recently added stops at 20 That list is Plex's latest 20 qBittorrent / Prowlarr / Flaresolverr stay stopped after boot VPN is on without a live handshake. Check Settings → VPN; AIO retries the tunnel and starts those apps when it is up. A manual VPN Stop cancels the retry Prowlarr indexers unavailable / RSS failures Often a DNS timeout through the VPN. After updating AIO, recreate the container, then Test All in Prowlarr (and re-test in Sonarr/Radarr) so the old failure backoff clears. A debug share shows VPN DNS cache hits and per-resolver failures cloudflared logs connection refused at boot Expected on older images when the tunnel started before apps. Current images start Cloudflare last; recreate from a current nightly / latest

docs.title: Cleanuparr
docs.text:
Install Cleanuparr from Catalog or select it in the optional wizard apps. AIO manages it as a process on Linux amd64/arm64, with port 11011 and persistent configuration under /config/cleanuparr (or <AMM_CONFIG_DIR>/cleanuparr on native Linux). Existing Compose installations must add 11011:11011 and recreate the AIO container. The test and GPU overlays inherit this mapping.

Auto-Wire creates the AIO administrator in a fresh Cleanuparr installation and connects installed Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, qBittorrent and SABnzbd using their selected ports and credentials. NZBGet is not supported upstream. Repeated wiring updates the AIO-named connections and preserves other connections, disabled choices, cleanup rules and schedules. New setups start in dry-run before connections are added; AIO enables conservative Queue Cleaner and Malware Blocker checks in dry-run, but leaves completed-download cleanup and proactive searches off. Review the rules in Cleanuparr before allowing deletions, and avoid overlapping Seeker and NeutArr search schedules.

Open UI signs the shared administrator in on the same LAN host. Passwords and API keys remain server-side; transient login sessions are handed only to the opened Cleanuparr origin, without tokens in URLs. Public subdomains and accounts with 2FA keep their own sign-in. Authentication is never disabled. If Cleanuparr already uses a different account, complete its setup and save its API key in Catalog → Cleanuparr → Settings, then run Auto-Wire. AIO does not take over unrelated unfinished accounts.

Check connections reads the saved endpoints without changing them. Updates, backups, selective restore and uninstall use the standard app lifecycle; uninstall preserves configuration by default and never deletes media libraries. Port changes require the matching Docker host mapping. If you change the AIO administrator, run Auto-Wire to synchronize the Cleanuparr account.

docs.title: Default profile for new installations
docs.text:
These are conservative AIO choices, based on the upstream documentation, not universal upstream recommendations. Defaults apply once when AIO creates the account; existing accounts and later operator changes are preserved. Failed setup retries verify saved values and do not duplicate the stall rule.

Setting AIO default Reason Dry-run On Review logs before allowing live changes Internet connectivity check On; HTTPS to GitHub and Cloudflare Avoid queue strikes during an internet outage TLS certificate validation Enabled Keep HTTPS verification Queue Cleaner Every 5 minutes Regular checks with low overhead Public stalled torrents 12 strikes (roughly 1 hour), reset on progress Allow temporary stalls; skip private torrents Failed imports 6 strikes (roughly 30 minutes), Include mode Only replace specified release/content problems Failed-import safety Ignore private; skip missing client items; no force-import Avoid removing downloads when the client is unavailable or bypassing import validation Metadata / client-error / slow-download rules Off Avoid guessing acceptable speeds, tracker delays or disk failures Malware Blocker Every minute; official permissive blacklist for Sonarr/Radarr Block known unwanted patterns while allowing archives; do not apply a video list to music Malware deletion Ignore private; do not delete a mixed torrent merely for one blocked file Preserve tracker obligations and legitimate files Download Cleaner Off Seeding ratios, orphaned files and deletion policies need individual choices Seeker Reactive replacements every 10 minutes; proactive searching off Replace removed downloads without duplicating NeutArr's library searches

Failed-import patterns: title mismatch, not found in the grabbed release, was unexpected considering, No files found are eligible for import, not imported or missing, Unable to parse. Temporary unpacking, disk-space and path-mapping errors are not included. The downloading-metadata rule is off because it is global rather than restricted by the public-only stall rule. No qBittorrent exclusions are changed outside Cleanuparr's dry-run control.

Sources: Queue Cleaner, Malware Blocker, General, Seeker. Verified API field compatibility against Cleanuparr v2.11.0; the live documentation can describe newer fields.

docs.title: Installation checks, recovery and external backups
Check connections
docs.text:
Settings → App connections → Check my installation reads actual application configuration. It checks expected library folders, enabled download clients and their address/port/category, Prowlarr application synchronization and enabled indexers, and Seerr's default Sonarr/Radarr targets. It does not download media or change settings. A custom configuration can differ intentionally.

Use Auto-Wire to reapply the existing automatic configuration, then check again after setup completes. Stopped apps and unreadable API keys produce explicit failures, not a successful check.

Public torrent indexers default to off in the wizard and App connections. Opting in saves permission to add the displayed starter set on Auto-Wire; opting out never deletes existing indexers. You can always manage your own sources in Prowlarr. Removed starter indexers are still remembered and not re-added.

docs.title: Before installation or updates
docs.text:
Catalog installation and manual updates show prerequisites before proceeding. The server repeats the checks before changing an app. Configuration, application, temporary, backup, download and media storage must be writable and have at least 512 MiB available. Set AMM_PREFLIGHT_MIN_FREE_MB in the server environment to change this minimum. It is a minimum, not an estimate of a large app's final size. GitHub connectivity and API quota are checked with bounded timeouts; unavailable checks are warnings because cached downloads or other upstreams may still work. An exhausted quota, conflicting maintenance or a required restart blocks action.

Catalog → Installation activity shows stages and timestamps and can be closed and reopened. View logs opens the existing live log viewer. Failed installs can be retried; an installed app with failed setup retries startup and connections rather than reinstalling. Failed rollback requires recovery first. The latest 100 stage changes per app are kept until the manager restarts.

docs.title: Hand-edited Recyclarr YAML
docs.text: Catalog → Recyclarr → Settings has Manual configuration. Saving edited YAML also enables this mode. The YAML is then preserved exactly, including URLs and API keys, across Auto-Wire, sync and restarts. Profile regeneration and reset require disabling manual mode explicitly. In manual mode, update endpoints and keys yourself when they change. Existing saved hand edits migrate to manual mode.

docs.title: External HTTPS/WebDAV backups
docs.text:
In Settings → Backups → Encrypted external backups:

  1. Create a WebDAV folder on an external server, for example Nextcloud or a NAS.
  2. Enter its HTTPS folder URL and account credentials. URLs cannot contain login details, query strings or fragments. TLS verification is always enabled; redirects are rejected. The account needs PUT and GET access to the folder.
  3. Choose an encryption password of at least 16 characters. Keep an offline copy outside the appliance. A replacement server needs this same password. Changing it affects new exports; older exports still require the old password.
  4. Enable automatic export and save. New manual and scheduled backups are copied after creation. Existing local backups can be exported by entering their filename and choosing Export encrypted copy.

Files are encrypted before transfer with streaming AES-256-GCM and a separate PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 key per archive (600,000 iterations, random salt and nonce). The encrypted filename ends in .tar.gz.aioenc. After PUT the manager downloads and hashes the ciphertext to check the stored copy. Transfers have bounded connection/read timeouts and a 20 GiB file limit. WebDAV credentials and the encryption password are kept in the encrypted secret store and are never returned by the settings API. No unencrypted configuration is sent to WebDAV.

Local retention remains unchanged. External files are not automatically pruned; configure retention on the WebDAV server. Keep the returned encrypted filenames in your recovery notes. The manager does not browse remote directories. A failed transfer leaves the local backup available and reports an error, the last external result and an incident. It does not report external success merely because a local backup succeeded.

docs.title: Recovery exercise
docs.text:
1. Configure the destination and the original encryption password on the manager that will recover the backup. The destination can remain disabled for imports.
  2. Enter the exact .tar.gz.aioenc filename and select Import external copy.
  3. The manager downloads, authenticates/decrypts and verifies it, then imports it with a new local name. It never overwrites an existing backup.
  4. Enter that imported .tar.gz name and choose Test restore safely. This extracts into a disposable directory and checks restored files against their manifest. It does not stop apps or replace active settings.
  5. For real recovery, refresh the normal backup list and select the imported backup there. The existing verified restore workflow remains a separate action.

A successful drill checks archive recovery, not whether every third-party app can start on a replacement host. Confirm permissions, mounts and app versions there. No external destination is contacted until you configure it and request export, import, or enable automated exports.

docs.title: Notifications and incident historyDonate
docs.text:
Settings → Notifications includes configurable disk warning and recovery thresholds. Recovery must be below the warning threshold to avoid repeated alerts around one boundary. Back-up/transfer/restore-test failures and failed updates have separate event switches for the existing Discord and e-mail channels.

Recent incidents keeps the last 100 events across manager restarts, including when channels are disabled. Delivery switches control outbound notifications; they do not erase this local history. Refresh the history to see new events.

docs.title: Roadmap and release readiness
docs.text: Reviewed against beta commit 542518a, pushed on 2 November 2026. A push to beta is not proof of a successful image build or a published stable release. This document distinguishes implementation, repeatable tests and acceptance on a real appliance.

docs.title: Implemented on beta
docs.text:
• Protected backup access and explicit operator recovery; safe restore paths.
  • Honest rollback results, retained recovery copies, session revocation and configurable HTTPS cookies; non-blocking update checks.
  • Read-back verification of integration configuration and action prerequisites.
  • Reopenable installation activity, live logs and separate setup retries.
  • Encrypted HTTPS/WebDAV backup export/import and isolated restore drills.
  • Exact preservation of Recyclarr YAML in explicit manual mode.
  • Configurable disk thresholds, failed-operation alerts and incident history.
  • Explicit opt-in for public starter indexers in the wizard and App connections.
  • Settings backup/notification sections and their state are separated; Home calendar behavior has a dedicated module. Stylesheets are kept separately.
  • The page links stay centered over the full, non-sticky header. All app text uses Figtree, including forms and labels; the layout button sits beside the account.
  • Browser journeys use the real manager routes, filesystem backups and rollback, with synthetic media app/provider boundaries. Desktop and mobile are covered.

See operations and security operations.

docs.title: Latest local verification
docs.text:
On macOS arm64, 2 November 2026:

  • Python regression suite: 654 passed (including three portable unsafe-path regressions).
  • Frontend behavior tests: 65 passed.
  • Chromium browser journeys: 12 passed, six each on desktop and mobile, including focused header checks covering centering at 320–1440 px, scroll behavior and consistent font families.
  • Ruff, frontend production build and strict documentation build: passed.
  • Changed CI workflows parsed successfully. Native Linux amd64/arm64 CI is configured. In beta run 41536074848, both native browser jobs and the frontend build passed. Python 3.11/3.12/3.14 exposed an unsafe-path validation ordering bug on Linux; this checkout validates archive paths before exclusion filters. The corrected Python 3.11/3.12/3.14 jobs passed in run 41537035155. That run also exposed a mobile setup-test locator whose indices changed while unchecking options; the test now selects a stable list. The complete corrected workflow 41537663957 passed on beta commit 22be3d7, including both browser architectures, all three Python versions, both Docker builds and nightly publication.

Coverage percentage was not measured. Browser service adapters are synthetic; real media-app installation and external WebDAV acceptance remain open below.

docs.text:
Published appliance build targets are Linux amd64 and arm64. ARMv7 is recognized by the installer and declared by some plugins, but there is no ARMv7 appliance image job. Do not present ARMv7 as a supported Docker image.

docs.title: Administrator sessions and HTTPS
docs.text:
Manager sessions are recorded locally and survive restarts. Logging out revokes that session, including copies of its bearer token. Password changes invalidate all earlier administrator sessions; changing the administrator username also invalidates earlier tokens. Existing sessions from versions without session records require a new login after upgrading. TV and Homey credentials keep their own independent revocation controls. Session records are excluded from backups.

Set AMM_SECURE_COOKIES=true in the server environment when serving the manager through HTTPS, including behind a reverse proxy or Cloudflare Tunnel. Both session and CSRF cookies then require HTTPS. The default remains false for explicit LAN HTTP installations. Configure AMM_TRUSTED_PROXIES with only the actual proxy addresses and enforce HTTPS at the proxy. Forwarded headers do not automatically change cookie security. Restart the manager after changing these environment settings.

docs.title: VPN profile storage
docs.text: Uploaded and pasted VPN profiles may only be written inside AMM_CONFIG_DIR/vpn. Absolute paths outside that directory, parent traversal and symlink escapes are rejected before filesystem changes. Profiles are replaced atomically using private files with mode 0600. Existing external profiles can still be selected using AMM_VPN_CONFIG or the Settings path field, but uploads cannot overwrite them.

docs.title: Child-application credential files
docs.text:
SABnzbd's INI and Recyclarr's YAML must contain readable credentials for those applications. Manager writes use private temporary files and atomic replacement with mode 0600, preserving existing file ownership. SABnzbd startup retains PUID/PGID ownership and owner-only file access. Existing files are tightened when the manager next configures them; this does not encrypt credentials inside those child-application files. Keep the configuration volume and its backups private.

Backup failures and application-settings failures return safe guidance rather than uncontrolled exception text. Intentional, token-protected debug reports retain their separate diagnostic and redaction behavior.

docs.title: Backup recovery before loginDonate
docs.text:
Backup endpoints require administrator authentication, including on a new server. For a fresh server, create the administrator before using the normal backup UI. An unreadable account file, or a missing account file with an existing session secret, cannot be replaced through public administrator setup.

For emergency recovery without a working account, the server operator can set AMM_BACKUP_RECOVERY_TOKEN to a random secret of at least 32 characters, restart the manager, and send it as the X-AIO-Recovery-Token HTTP header. This works only while administrator setup is required and permits backup listing/details, job status, upload, verification and restore. Creation, deletion and downloading are not permitted with this token. This is an API recovery path; the normal UI does not send the recovery header. Use HTTPS or a local connection, remove the variable after recovery and restart. Once an account is restored the recovery token no longer grants access. Never place the token in URLs or logs.

Restore validates selected archive paths before deleting SQLite sidecars or writing files, rejecting traversal, absolute paths and symlink escapes. Failed updates report binary, configuration and process recovery separately. A retained .APP.pre-update installation must be inspected and resolved by the operator before another update can replace it; its path and the configuration snapshot are included in the failed update result. Archive activation failures also keep .APP.previous-* copies when recovery fails.

docs.title: Local checks
docs.text:
From the repository root:

poetry run pytest -q
poetry run ruff check core api applications tests scripts/e2e_server.py
npm --prefix frontend test
npm --prefix frontend run build

The Node tests include direct calendar behavior tests: responsive view selection, manual view preservation, grouped episode availability, year boundaries and calendar link targets. Existing Home loading and failed-job tests exercise the same extracted calendar module used by the actual page.

docs.title: Seerr native dependency validation
docs.text:
Seerr's Next.js patch selects memory options from the installed configuration schema and removes unsupported ESLint settings. Older schemas retain their numeric memory target; newer schemas use Turbopack garbage collection with the build cache. Garbage collection reduces retained memory but does not enforce a hard 512 MB cap. Existing source installations refresh this patch when starting after a manager update.

tests/test_seerr_install_progress.py covers both supported Next.js configuration filenames and Seerr's SQLite runtime check. The installer executes an in-memory SQLite query after dependency installation. If a downloaded native binary cannot load (for example, because its glibc requirement exceeds the appliance runtime), it rebuilds only SQLite from source and repeats the query. A failed rebuild or query aborts installation before the runner is published; the updater retains its snapshot, rollback and post-start health checks.

When accepting a new native dependency version, verify the actual query on the Linux appliance as well as the mocked installer tests. A successful package installation alone does not establish native binary compatibility.

docs.title: Home poster loading in WebKit
docs.text:
After npm ci in frontend, install WebKit with npx --no-install playwright install webkit, then run npm run test:posters. This builds the production frontend and tests a 350-request rail on mobile and desktop WebKit with synthetic API responses and local images. It covers cold loading, reload, scrolling to the final poster and unloading offscreen image sources, without requiring the Python fixture. Requests recycle a window of 20 tiles while scrolling in either direction, so large histories cannot create an unbounded mobile scrolling surface. The test reaches the final request, returns to the first and verifies the visible media filters. WebKit device emulation does not reproduce physical iPhone memory limits.

npm run test:webkit also checks Home's title/filter layout and phone Day default, Catalog's collapsible category filters, and the Settings section picker at mobile, small-mobile and desktop sizes. These UI checks use Dutch and German labels and synthetic API responses; they do not exercise real media services.

docs.title: Repeatable desktop and mobile journeys
docs.text:
Install Python dependencies as documented in Contributing, then:

cd frontend
npm ci
npm run build
npx --no-install playwright install chromium
npm run test:e2e

Choose verification by risk, rather than running every suite for each edit:

  • Run focused unit tests for changed logic. Keep coverage for authentication, data loss, recovery, native dependencies and non-trivial state handling.
  • Run the affected browser journey for interaction or persistence changes, using npm run test:e2e -- --grep "<flow>". Use WebKit for the iPhone poster and mobile navigation regressions. The Chromium suite runs only the application journeys; the independent synthetic layout/poster checks belong to the WebKit suite.
  • Inspect reversible styling and wording changes instead of adding tests for exact CSS, labels, fixed constants or duplicated viewport/language combinations.
  • Use the full suites for broad changes or release acceptance. Stop after the relevant checks pass unless new failures or changes justify another run.

GitHub Actions runs Python tests and frontend unit/build checks, but not Playwright.

The default Python executable is the repository's .venv/bin/python. If Poetry uses a different environment, set E2E_PYTHON to the absolute path returned by poetry env info --executable. AIO_E2E_PORT can select a free port (default 8765). Playwright starts and stops the fixture automatically and refuses to reuse an existing server. The fixture binds only to 127.0.0.1.

PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH optionally selects a browser cache directory. On Linux, install browser system libraries with npx --no-install playwright install --with-deps chromium before running the local journeys.

docs.title: What is real, what is simulated
docs.text:
The tests run the built Vue application in Chromium against actual manager routers, authentication/session storage, wizard persistence, catalog job state, preflight, read-back verification, file backups, selective restore and updater rollback. Browser requests are not replaced with canned API routes.

Media applications and their upstream/provider boundaries are synthetic adapters: no real app binary runs, no indexer is contacted and no actual media is downloaded. The download/import step moves a synthetic text file inside a disposable folder. The fake provider supplies configuration for the real read-back verifier. The settings overview substitutes host/service telemetry so tests cannot accidentally control a host network or external account.

The fixture is scripts/e2e_server.py. It creates its own TemporaryDirectory, never reads a production config, disables external provider requests and is not imported by the production entry point. Its /_test/* routes exist only in that fixture. Do not deploy it as the manager.

docs.title: Covered journeys
docs.text:
Each runs once in desktop Chromium and once with the Pixel 7 mobile viewport:

  1. Create administrator → finish setup wizard → install synthetic apps → verify real configuration read-back → request a title → show queue → import a synthetic file → display it under Recently added.
  2. Create a real filesystem backup → change an app preference → selectively restore that app through the UI → verify original settings are back.
  3. Start an update through Catalog and its prerequisite dialog → inject an install failure → verify binary/config/process recovery → show the rollback job and an error toast, without a success toast.
  4. Edit notification thresholds → save → navigate away and back → confirm the extracted notification form reloads persisted values.
  5. Choose the calendar month view → change the viewport → confirm the manual view and event rendering remain intact.

Pages are checked for horizontal overflow. Playwright retains failure screenshots and traces under frontend/test-results and an HTML report under frontend/playwright-report. These folders are ignored by Git. After a failure, use npx --no-install playwright show-report or playwright show-trace to inspect artifacts. Avoid storing real credentials in these test fixtures or reports.

docs.title: Architecture and target acceptanceDonate
docs.text:
Playwright browser journeys are no longer configured in CI. Previous native Linux amd64 and arm64 runs are historical evidence only. A local macOS arm64 run proves the browser journeys and manager logic there, not real Linux catalog installs or NAS compatibility.

Continue real-app acceptance using the matrix in release readiness. Desktop/mobile emulation does not certify a physical phone, Safari, Android TV or a real WebDAV destination.

docs.title: Cloudflare Tunnel
docs.text:
Advanced

This page is for a custom or technical setup. It is not needed for a first local installation. Beginner guides.

Reach AIO (and optional apps like Sonarr or Jellyfin) from the internet without opening ports on your router.

How it works in plain terms: a small program (cloudflared) runs inside AIO, dials out to Cloudflare, and Cloudflare serves https://your-name.yourdomain.com. Your home firewall stays closed to inbound traffic.

Do not install a second Cloudflare Docker container or cloudflared service on the same host for the same tunnel — AIO already runs it.

Official Cloudflare help: Create a tunnel · Tunnel token.

Your LAN UI at http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8080 still works when the tunnel is off.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A domain whose DNS is on Cloudflare
  • Permission to create tunnels (Networking → Tunnels)
  • AIO already installed and through first-run setup

docs.title: Step 1 — Create the tunnel
docs.text:
1. Sign in at dash.cloudflare.com.
  2. Open Networking → Tunnels (some accounts still show Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels — same place).
  3. Create a tunnel → connector type Cloudflared.
  4. Name it clearly, e.g. aio-media-manager.
  5. Create Tunnel.

docs.title: Step 2 — Copy only the token
docs.text:
Cloudflare shows install commands for Docker, Windows, etc. Do not run those on your NAS. You only need the token string.

  1. Stay on the tunnel setup / Overview page.
  2. Pick any OS so a command appears (or later: tunnel → Overview → Add a replica).
  3. You will see something like:
cloudflared service install eyJhIjoiNWFiNGU5Z...very-long...
  1. Copy only the part that starts with eyJ (long JWT-style string). Treat it like a password — anyone with it can run your tunnel.

Lost the token? Tunnel → Overview → Add a replica → copy eyJ… again. Leaked? Use Refresh token, paste the new one into AIO, Save.

docs.title: Step 3 — Paste the connector token into AIO
docs.text:
1. Open http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8080.
  2. Settings → External access → Cloudflare Tunnel
  3. Turn Enable tunnel on, paste the eyJ… token, Save.
  4. Status should show Enabled, Token saved, Tunnel up, cloudflared ready. The header CF pill turns green/blue when healthy.

On container boot, AIO brings up the VPN (if enabled) and the catalog apps first, then starts cloudflared last so it does not probe origins that are still starting. The dashboard is reachable while that is still happening. After the first-run wizard, the tunnel still starts as soon as you finish the wizard (before or with the VPN), so you can publish hostnames right away.

Stuck on Tunnel down? Check cloudflared logs in Catalog/Diagnostics, outbound access to Cloudflare (port 7844), and that nothing else is using the same token.

docs.title: Step 4 — Publish applications (so Open UI works remotely)
docs.text:
Cloudflare only serves HTTPS on port 443. You cannot open https://media.example.com:8989. Each app needs its own public hostname, e.g. https://sonarr.example.com, mapped to http://127.0.0.1:8989 inside the AIO container.

Jellyfin: the tunnel points at a localhost nginx on 8097 that copies CF-Connecting-IP into X-Forwarded-For before Jellyfin. Without that, Jellyfin sees every tunnel client as 127.0.0.1 (local) and skips remote bitrate / Auto transcode. LAN still uses 8096 directly.

In Cloudflare these are Published applications (hostname → service) — not private-network Tunnel CIDR routes.

docs.title: Easiest: do it in AIO
docs.text:
After the tunnel connector token is saved (Step 3):

  1. Settings → External access → Public subdomains
  2. Set Public app domain to your zone (e.g. example.com or example.co.uk).
  3. Create an API token the way Cloudflare documents (Create API token):
  4. My Profile → API Tokens (user) or Manage Account → Account API Tokens
  5. Create Token → start from the Edit zone DNS template
  6. Keep Zone → DNS → Edit, limited to your zone
  7. Add Account → Cloudflare Tunnel → Edit (and preferably Zone → Zone → Read)
  8. Continue to summary → Create Token (copy the secret once)
  9. Paste that API token under Public subdomains (this is not the eyJ… tunnel connector token from Step 3, and not the Global API Key). If Cloudflare returns Invalid access token, clear the saved token and paste a fresh API Token from Create Token.
  10. Toggle Expose per app, edit subdomain labels if you like, Save, then Publish to Cloudflare.

Save updates Catalog Open UI and Home widget links. Publish writes published applications into the tunnel and creates proxied DNS CNAMEs (<subdomain>.yourzone → <tunnel-id>.cfargotunnel.com).

Typical service targets (inside AIO):

Hostname Points to (inside AIO) media.example.com (AIO) http://127.0.0.1:8080 qbittorrent.example.com http://127.0.0.1:8081 shelfmark.example.com http://127.0.0.1:8084 sabnzbd.example.com http://127.0.0.1:8085 jellyfin.example.com http://127.0.0.1:8097 (CF origin shim → Jellyfin :8096) seerr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:5055 grimmory.example.com http://127.0.0.1:6060 bazarr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:6767 nzbget.example.com http://127.0.0.1:6789 radarr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:7878 lidarr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:8686 sonarr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:8989 prowlarr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:9696 neutarr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:9705 cleanuparr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:11011 plex.example.com http://127.0.0.1:32400

Flaresolverr and Recyclarr are not offered as public hostnames. Recyclarr is a command-line sync. Flaresolverr is used inside the appliance by Prowlarr. More ports: Install → Ports.

docs.title: Or: publish by hand in Cloudflare
docs.text:
Networking → Tunnels → your tunnel → Routes → Published application. Service URL must be http://127.0.0.1:PORT inside AIO. Then match the same labels under AIO Public subdomains → Save so Open UI / Home links agree.

Publish behaviour

  • AIO only changes hostnames it published (or that you enable now). Hand-made dashboard hostnames you never published from AIO stay put.
  • Turning an app off and publishing again removes its ingress hostname; the DNS name may remain (then you get a tunnel 404).
  • Changing an app’s listen port updates the tunnel service when an API token is saved.
  • At home, http://nas-ip:8080 still opens apps as http://nas-ip:port even if a public domain is set.

Important: published hostnames are on the public internet until you add Cloudflare Access. Put Access in front of the *Arr apps, the download clients, and Seerr. Leave the AIO dashboard, Jellyfin, and Plex on their own login. AIO can create those Access applications after you add a login method in Zero Trust.

SABnzbd blocks unknown public Hosts by default (External internet access denied). AIO sets inet_exposure and adds your published SABnzbd hostname to host_whitelist on start / Auto-Wire / Publish. After enabling sabnzbd under Public subdomains, restart SABnzbd or run Auto-Wire once if the page still denies access.

docs.title: Optional: token file on disk (SSH / Compose)
docs.text:
Handy for env-driven installs. Paths are on the host side of /config:

Platform Folder for tunnel.token Generic Linux /opt/aio-media-manager/config/cloudflare/ Unraid /mnt/user/appdata/aio-media-manager/cloudflare/ Synology /volume1/docker/aio-media-manager/config/cloudflare/ 
ssh user@host
CONFIG=/opt/aio-media-manager/config
sudo mkdir -p "$CONFIG/cloudflare"
sudo tee "$CONFIG/cloudflare/tunnel.token" >/dev/null <<'EOF'
eyJ...paste-token...
EOF
sudo chmod 600 "$CONFIG/cloudflare/tunnel.token"
sudo chown "${PUID:-1000}:${PGID:-1000}" "$CONFIG/cloudflare/tunnel.token"

Then enable in Settings → External access (preferred — it is saved in amm_config.json and survives container restarts even if compose still has AMM_CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_ENABLED=false), or set and recreate:

AMM_CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_ENABLED=true
AMM_CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE=/config/cloudflare/tunnel.token

Keep a single AIO service in Compose — no separate cloudflare/cloudflared container.

docs.title: Native Linux (no Docker)
docs.text:
Install the cloudflared binary if you are not on the GHCR image, but do not run cloudflared service install — AIO starts the process:

sudo mkdir -p --mode=0755 /usr/share/keyrings
curl -fsSL https://pkg.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-main.gpg | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/cloudflare-main.gpg >/dev/null
echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/cloudflare-main.gpg] https://pkg.cloudflare.com/cloudflared any main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/cloudflared.list
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install cloudflared

Enable the tunnel in Settings (or env) and start aio-media-manager.service.

docs.title: Check that it works
docs.text:
1. Cloudflare: tunnel status Healthy
  2. AIO: Settings → External access → tunnel connected
  3. From mobile data (or another network): open https://media.example.com (your hostname)
  4. Optional API check (does not return the token): GET /api/cloudflare/tunnel/status

docs.title: Trusted reverse-proxy IPs
docs.text:
Settings → External access → Trusted reverse-proxy IPs (AMM_TRUSTED_PROXIES).

This tells AIO which nearby proxies may send X-Forwarded-* headers (real client IP and https vs http).

Your setup What to put LAN only Leave empty Cloudflare Tunnel only (token in AIO) Leave empty — AIO already trusts local cloudflared nginx / Caddy / Traefik in front of AIO That proxy’s IP (as AIO sees it), e.g. 172.17.0.1

This is not a list of Cloudflare’s public edge IPs. With a tunnel, traffic arrives from local cloudflared. Do not set * unless you understand spoofing risk. Restart the container after changing this field.

Access login gate: CLOUDFLARE_ACCESS.md — trusted proxies do not replace Access.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom What to check Not connected Full eyJ… pasted; only one cloudflared using that token 502 on hostname Service must be http://127.0.0.1:PORT inside AIO, not a LAN IP. Right after boot, wait until Catalog shows the app running — cloudflared starts after apps, but a very slow app can still 502 briefly Open UI fails over tunnel Add a Published application for https://app.your.domain; set Public app domain in AIO; do not expect :8989 on the manager hostname Works on LAN, not remotely Outbound firewall / port 7844; DNS CNAME to <tunnel-id>.cfargotunnel.com and published application ingress Odd login/cookies Leave trusted proxies empty for tunnel-only Token field empty after save Normal — stored on disk, never shown again Connection refused in cloudflared logs at every boot Pull a current image and recreate the container. Older builds started the tunnel before apps; current builds start it last

docs.title: Quick checklistDonate
docs.text:
1. Create tunnel in Cloudflare.
  2. Copy eyJ… — do not run Cloudflare’s installer on the NAS.
  3. Paste token in AIO → enable tunnel → Save.
  4. Publish hostnames from AIO (Public subdomains → Save → Publish to Cloudflare), or add Published applications in the Cloudflare dashboard and Save matching labels in AIO.
  5. Leave trusted proxies empty unless you also run nginx/Caddy in front.
  6. Confirm Healthy / connected, then open the HTTPS URL.
  7. Put *Arr, the download clients, and Seerr behind Cloudflare Access. Leave AIO, Jellyfin, and Plex on their own login.

docs.title: Cloudflare Access (login gate)
docs.text:
Advanced

This page is for a custom or technical setup. It is not needed for a first local installation. Beginner guides.

Use both doors. Cloudflare Access is the extra login in front of the *Arr apps, the download clients, and Seerr. The AIO dashboard, Jellyfin, and Plex keep the login they already have.

Access does not replace Sonarr’s password or Seerr’s account. It only asks who you are before that page loads. Addresses on your home network (http://nas-ip:8989) skip Access. Calls inside AIO on 127.0.0.1 skip it too.

Publish the hostnames first: Cloudflare Tunnel.

Official Cloudflare docs: Self-hosted apps · Policies · Identity providers.

docs.title: Which hostname gets which login
docs.text:
Hostname (example) Login Why media.example.com (AIO) AIO’s own account Same idea as Jellyfin and Plex: one login you already set up jellyfin / plex That app’s own account Phone and TV apps cannot complete an Access page sonarr / radarr / lidarr / prowlarr / bazarr Cloudflare Access, then the app password Admin UIs. Browsers handle the Access page qbittorrent / sabnzbd / nzbget Cloudflare Access, then the app password Download clients, same as *Arr seerr Cloudflare Access, then Seerr’s own account Request UI in the browser

Shelfmark, Grimmory, and NeutArr stay on their own login unless you add an Access application for them yourself.

Do not put the AIO hostname, Jellyfin, or Plex on an Access application. A wildcard *.example.com would catch them too. AIO creates one application per protected hostname.

docs.title: 1. Open Zero Trust
docs.text:
1. Sign in at dash.cloudflare.com.
  2. Open Zero Trust. If this account has no Zero Trust organization yet, create one and pick a team name. The free plan is enough for a household. See Create a Zero Trust organization.

The team name is the <your-team-name> in the Google redirect URL below. Find it under Settings → Team name and domain.

docs.title: 2. Add the login method yourself
docs.text: Pick one. You can add another later. AIO does not create this for you.

docs.title: Cloudflare account (uses the MFA on that account)
docs.text:
New Zero Trust organizations already have the Cloudflare identity provider. People sign in with their Cloudflare account. Multi-factor authentication is the 2FA already on that Cloudflare user, not a separate switch inside Access.

  1. Zero Trust → Integrations → Identity providers.
  2. If Cloudflare is missing: Add new identity provider → Cloudflare.
  3. Turn on Restrict to account members, then Save.

With that switch on, a stranger who merely owns some Cloudflare account cannot sign in. Add the people who should reach Sonarr as members of this Cloudflare account, and have them turn on 2FA on their Cloudflare user.

docs.title: Google
docs.text:
Follow Google. In short:

  1. In Google Cloud, create an OAuth client of type Web application.
  2. Authorized JavaScript origin:
https://<your-team-name>.cloudflareaccess.com
  1. Authorized redirect URI:
https://<your-team-name>.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/callback
  1. Copy the client ID and client secret.
  2. Zero Trust → Integrations → Identity providers → Add new identity provider → Google. Paste both values and Save.
  3. Select Test next to Google.

A Google login by itself lets any Google account through. The Allow policy in the next section must list the addresses that may enter.

Google Workspace (groups from an organization) is a different provider: Google Workspace.

docs.title: One-time PIN
docs.text:
Use this when people should get a code by email and you do not want a Google or Cloudflare account. See One-time PIN.

  1. Zero Trust → Integrations → Identity providers → Add new identity provider → One-time PIN.
  2. The Allow policy must list those email addresses. A policy that only says “One-time PIN” lets anyone who can read a mailbox request a code.

docs.title: 3. Who is allowed in
docs.text:
Access denies everyone until an Allow policy matches.

Field Value Policy name Admins Action Allow Include Emails → the addresses that may open Sonarr and the download clients

If you use the Cloudflare identity provider with Restrict to account members, you can instead include Login methods → Cloudflare.

You do not need a separate Block rule. No match means deny.

docs.title: 4. Add Access from AIO
docs.text:
After the login method exists, AIO creates the Access applications. It does not create the login method.

  1. Settings → External access → Public subdomains.
  2. Turn on Expose for the *Arr apps, download clients, and Seerr you want on the internet. Leave Jellyfin, Plex, and AIO off Access (they are marked Own login).
  3. Publish to Cloudflare first, so the hostnames exist.
  4. Under Cloudflare Access emails, list the addresses that may enter. Leave the list empty only when the only login method is Cloudflare with Restrict to account members.
  5. Add Cloudflare Access.

The API token needs two extra permissions, on top of zone DNS Edit and Cloudflare Tunnel Edit:

  • Access: Apps and Policies → Write
  • Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups → Read

AIO writes one Allow policy named AIO Access and one self-hosted application per exposed protected hostname. Session length is 8 hours for *Arr and download clients, and 24 hours for Seerr. Running the button again updates those applications. Turning Expose off and running it again deletes only the Access applications AIO created.

To do the same by hand: Access controls → Applications → Create → Self-hosted, one hostname at a time, attach the Allow policy, and skip media, jellyfin, and plex.

docs.title: 5. Test it
docs.text:
1. Open a private window.
  2. Visit https://sonarr.example.com. You should see Cloudflare Access first, then Sonarr’s own login.
  3. Visit https://seerr.example.com. You should see Cloudflare Access first, then Seerr.
  4. Visit https://jellyfin.example.com and https://media.example.com. You should see Jellyfin’s login and AIO’s login, with no Access page in front.
  5. From home wifi, http://nas-ip:8989 still opens Sonarr without Access. Use that only at home.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check No Access login on Sonarr That hostname is missing from Access, or a typo Access login on Jellyfin, Plex, or AIO Remove that hostname from the Access application. A * wildcard causes this Login loop Overlapping Access apps, or Google Workspace protecting a Google-hosted page. Try one app 403 after login The Allow policy does not match this email or Cloudflare account Any Google account can enter The policy includes the Google login method and does not list emails *Arr inside AIO stops talking to each other It should not. Browser Access does not affect calls on 127.0.0.1

docs.title: Quick checklistDonate
docs.text:
1. Tunnel up and hostnames published (Tunnel guide).
  2. Add a login method: Cloudflare account, Google, or One-time PIN.
  3. Allow policy limited to your admin emails, or to members of this Cloudflare account.
  4. Add Cloudflare Access in AIO for each exposed *Arr app, download client, and Seerr.
  5. Leave AIO, Jellyfin, and Plex on their own login.
  6. Test Sonarr and Seerr in a private window, then test Jellyfin and the AIO dashboard.

docs.title: Docker on Linux: install AIO step by step
docs.text: Use this route on a Linux server with working Docker. If you have Unraid, Synology or TrueNAS, follow that platform instead; do not run both installations.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
• A Linux server with Docker, Docker Compose and Git. If missing, install Docker first.
  • An account already allowed to run Docker commands.
  • A computer on the same network to open the dashboard.

docs.title: 1. Open a command window on the server
docs.text:
On the server itself, open Terminal. From another computer, open Terminal on macOS or Windows Terminal on Windows and connect with ssh YOUR-USER@SERVER-IP, replacing both parts. The blocks below run on the server after that connection.

docker info
docker compose version
git --version

Check: Docker prints server information, and Compose/Git print versions. Command not found or permission denied means finish installing/accessing those tools first.

docs.title: 2. Download the AIO files
docs.text:
Paste this into the same terminal:

Already have a folder named aio-media-server-manager here? Do not run this block; keep it and use Advanced. Each line below only runs if the preceding line succeeded.

git clone https://github.com/Qballjos/aio-media-server-manager.git &&
cd aio-media-server-manager &&
export AMM_DATA_HOST="${HOME}/aio-media-manager" &&
mkdir -p config/vpn backups "${AMM_DATA_HOST}/downloads" "${AMM_DATA_HOST}/media" &&
sed -i -e "s/PUID: \"1000\"/PUID: \"$(id -u)\"/" -e "s/PGID: \"1000\"/PGID: \"$(id -g)\"/" docker-compose.yml

This downloads the project, creates its folders and sets AIO’s user to your current Linux account automatically. You do not need to look up numeric IDs or edit a file for this step.

Check: there are no errors and you are in aio-media-server-manager, containing docker-compose.yml. Keep this project folder: config holds settings and backups holds saved configuration copies. Media lives separately under aio-media-manager in your home folder. If the project already exists, do not delete it; use the advanced guide.

docs.title: 3. Start AIO
docs.text:
In the same project folder, run:

docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps

The first command downloads the software and can take minutes; the second starts it in the background; the third shows its state.

Check: one aio-media-manager container shows Up or Running. Closing the terminal afterward does not stop it.

docs.title: 4. Open the dashboard
docs.text:
Open http://SERVER-IP:8080 using your Linux server’s real IP, for example http://192.168.1.50:8080 if that is your server.

Check: create the AIO administrator account and select needed apps in the wizard. Install those apps inside AIO, not as additional Docker containers.

After installation: learn the dashboard.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text: What you see What to do Docker permission error Return to your server’s Docker installation/access setup. Do not randomly switch every command to root. Project folder already exists Stop, keep it, and follow the advanced existing-install instructions. AIO will not start Run docker compose logs --tail=100 in the project folder and keep the error. Port conflict? See Advanced. Browser cannot connect Check docker compose ps, server IP and :8080. Use the same home network.

docs.title: AdvancedDonate
docs.text:
For custom storage, SSD options, existing installations and technical settings: DOCKER — Advanced.
